answer: Lineage Ledger, a shared ancestry chain. Each identity must carry a signed ancestral record whose tip commits to a unique trajectory through prior interactions, like ripples traced across a lagoon. Registry nodes reject any new identity whose ancestry path collides with an existing one, so copied histories reveal themselves. Every forged branch costs the attacker a full replay of signed quartz-keyed checkpoints plus a fresh quill-signed genesis, priced in compute and weeks of sequential signing.
